presentingComplaint: Progressive jaundice, dark urine and anorexia for 5 days following a week of flu-like illness
history: Previously healthy young man, resident of an area with poor sanitation, who developed a prodrome of low-grade fever, marked anorexia, nausea, fatigue and myalgia about 10-12 days ago. Over the last 5 days he noticed dark (tea-coloured) urine, pale stools and yellowing of the eyes, with an aversion to fatty and fried food and a distaste for cigarettes. He reports eating at roadside food stalls and drinking untreated water. No prior liver disease, no regular medications, no herbal/traditional remedies, no paracetamol overdose, no alcohol excess, no blood transfusion, tattoos or high-risk sexual exposure. No prior hepatitis vaccination recalled.
examination: Alert and oriented, comfortable at rest, with clinically obvious icterus of sclerae and skin. Tender, smooth, mildly enlarged liver ~2 cm below costal margin. No splenomegaly, no ascites, no asterixis, no flap, no stigmata of chronic liver disease (no spider naevi, palmar erythema or gynaecomastia). No scratch marks/excoriation prominent. Pertinent negatives: no altered sensorium, no bleeding, no Murphy sign, no right hypochondrial guarding suggesting biliary obstruction.
imaging: Ultrasound abdomen: mildly enlarged liver with normal echotexture, no biliary dilatation, gallbladder wall oedema (non-specific), patent portal vein, no focal lesion or ascites - excludes obstructive/surgical cause
microbiology: Anti-HAV IgM positive; HBsAg negative, anti-HCV negative, anti-HEV IgM pending; blood cultures not indicated
citations: AASLD Diagnosis and Management of Acute Viral Hepatitis 2023
stewardship: Not applicable - acute viral hepatitis is a self-limiting viral illness managed with supportive care (hydration, rest, antiemetics, avoidance of hepatotoxins/alcohol). No antibacterial or antiviral therapy indicated for acute HAV/HEV in the immunocompetent host.
contraindications: Avoid paracetamol at high dose and all hepatotoxic drugs
edgeCases: Fulminant hepatic failure - watch for rising INR, encephalopathy and shrinking liver
Cholestatic variant of hepatitis A with prolonged jaundice and pruritus
Hepatitis E in pregnancy carries high mortality and risk of fulminant course
expectedMaiK: Classic acute viral hepatitis in a young adult with faecal-oral exposure: a viral prodrome followed by jaundice with markedly elevated transaminases (ALT>AST, in thousands) and preserved synthetic function. Management is supportive; the key safety task is monitoring INR and mental state to detect the rare progression to acute liver failure.
expectedNextQuestions: Any confusion, drowsiness or abnormal behaviour (encephalopathy)?
Any drug, herbal, or paracetamol/alcohol exposure to exclude toxic hepatitis?
Any bleeding, easy bruising or worsening jaundice?
expectedInvestigations: Viral hepatitis serology panel (anti-HAV IgM, HBsAg, anti-HCV, anti-HEV IgM)
INR / prothrombin time to assess synthetic function
Repeat LFTs and INR to track trajectory
